p1jzle1.s: Greenpoint coffee shop on Kent Street that mixes coffee with art and philosophy. It has since added an Upper East Side location.

p17635d3.s: Greenpoint's most buzzed-about bakery, worth the line for viral croissants and inventive riffs on classic pastries.

p1ybrhz0.s: East Village bakery and cafe on East 3rd Street, a cheap and easy neighborhood staple. It closed in April 2026 after 16 years.

p1smqy8x.s: Listening room and tea room upstairs on the Bowery, built for quiet, focused listening.

pb886pe.s: East Village Italian pastry shop since 1894, famous for cannoli, cheesecake and gelato.

p1n07t8v.s: Upper East Side kosher bakery since 1946, home to what many call New York's best black-and-white cookie.

p18aw3wb.s: Tribeca vinyl listening bar in the former 87 Walker space, with a room "where the music does the talking".

p1m8gszk.s: Harlem's legendary 125th Street theater, celebrating 90 years of music, art and theater, and home of the famous Amateur Night.

p13bafvd.s: Lower East Side live-music bar with bands every night, one of the earliest rock venues south of Houston Street. On rock-and-roll karaoke nights, you're the entertainment.

p1ff8g7l.s: Famous jazz club named for Charlie "Bird" Parker, now on West 44th Street in the Theater District, with big bands and top names most nights.

pak123v.s: Greenwich Village jazz club billing itself "the jazz capital of the world", where legends share the bill with young talent, with dinner and a full bar.

pgg3g2d.s: Midtown concert hall open since 1891, where everyone from Gershwin and Louis Armstrong to the Beatles has played.

p168gpc7.s: 250-capacity music and performance venue under Chelsea Market, opened in 2018, hosting concerts, dance, comedy and immersive theater.

pm98a56.s: Multi-room Bushwick music venue and club with dance parties on its roof.

p1ogdgak.s: No-frills DIY venue in Ridgewood with a balanced mix of local and international electronic acts.

pc9aund.s: Huge art and music venue in a 1903 factory in Maspeth, Queens, home to adventurous exhibitions, concerts and the Basement club.

p1ukqgm1.s: Alphabet City music club marked only by a blue light, with jazz, global grooves and late-night dancing.

p1v9j39s.s: Devon Turnbull's acoustically tuned OJAS listening room inside the USM showroom, his first semi-permanent space.

p1vuttlm.s: Bushwick jazz club with vegan food, a roof deck and no cover, where musicians come to experiment.

p8yw20q.s: Vinyl listening lounge in Long Island City that opened in May 2023 and quickly became one of the city's must-visit bars.

panzbh3.s: Basement Japanese jazz bar and izakaya in Midtown East, one of the area's coolest date spots, with live sets nightly and a small cover.

pwnahu3.s: Greenwich Village jazz club opened by Max Gordon in 1935 and devoted to jazz since 1957, still one of the great rooms in the world.

p1su0id7.s: Garment District shop for DJs, celebrating 50 years, with vinyl across hip-hop, R&B, reggae, house and more, plus pro DJ gear.

pysdboj.s: Tiny Greenwich Village record store run by Jamal Alsnar, where you might bump into a celebrity crate-digging.

pqbwzl5.s: Smithsonian's design museum in the Andrew Carnegie Mansion on Museum Mile.

p11tqiui.s: The Frick Collection's temporary home in the Breuer building (2021–2024). The Frick has since returned to its renovated Fifth Avenue mansion, which reopened in 2025.

p1mgm07k.s: Larry Gagosian's blue-chip contemporary art gallery, with big shows in its West 24th Street spaces in Chelsea and on Madison Avenue.

p1noqe36.s: New York space of London's Lisson Gallery, a leading contemporary art gallery since 1967 that has shown Ai Weiwei and Marina Abramović.

p1m2md56.s: Columbus Circle museum telling stories through craft, art and design.

pdxjsru.s: Contemporary art gallery founded by Jeanne Greenberg Rohatyn, known for its Upper East Side townhouse spaces.

p6jcyh1.s: Frank Lloyd Wright's spiraling museum on Fifth Avenue, part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site, with modern and contemporary art.

p10usmff.s: Art and design gallery from Nacho Polo and Robert Onuska, which opened in 2024 in a striking space at Church and Leonard in Tribeca.

p24bhxa.s: The Met: 5,000 years of art from every corner of the world, too big for one visit.

p1k4kdv5.s: MoMA on West 53rd Street, home to modern masterpieces and the art of our time.

p1b2a8e1.s: Museum of American art in a Renzo Piano building in the Meatpacking District at the foot of the High Line, opened in 2015.

p1tjya6n.s: Tranquil Japanese bookstore cafe in DUMBO with a lovely matcha latte.

p12u0gje.s: Natural history museum on Central Park West: the 94-foot blue whale, dinosaur skeletons and famous dioramas.

p1w1gxy.s: Manhattan's 843-acre backyard of lawns, woods, lakes and landmarks.

pbjqi7i.s: The classic photo spot on Washington Street in DUMBO, where the Manhattan Bridge frames the Empire State Building.

p1m64jo5.s: Far West Side development at the top of the High Line, with the Edge observation deck, The Shed, the Vessel and a mall.

p1gdnex.s: The tallest building in the Western Hemisphere, at the World Trade Center, with an observatory near the top.

p1nefje1.s: Aerial tram over the East River to Roosevelt Island, a cheap, scenic ride with skyline views.

p1bj41or.s: College founded by Peter Cooper in 1859. Its landmark Foundation Building and Great Hall have hosted famous speeches, including Lincoln's in 1860.
